subject: Unexpected 429 spike — config drift, recovery steps and next actions
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Stone <alex.stone@orchidanalytics.com>, ops@orchidanalytics.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected 429s from Orchid — initial notice

Hi Alex,

Thanks for the heads up over the phone — I’m following up in writing so we have a thread. We’re seeing a spike of 429 responses originating from requests that previously succeeded for Orchid Analytics between ~08:50–09:10 PDT. Early indicators show the errors are coming from our rate-limiter rejecting traffic with a new policy key (more below).

Immediate impact you reported: several sync jobs failing (status 429), user-facing features retrying and creating duplicate entries, and delays in onboarding flows.

I’ve looped in Karthik (serving/runtime) and Neha (Customer Success) to triage and coordinate. We’ll:
- Confirm root cause and timeline
- Provide mitigation steps you can apply immediately
- Share a recovery plan and follow up with a short postmortem and configuration diff

Could you share (if available) a single successful request ID around 08:45 and a failed request ID around 09:00? That will speed the trace. If you don’t have IDs, a short log snippet or symptom list is fine.

Thanks — I’ll follow up in 30–45 mins with findings.

Regards,
Soojin Lee
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

- UI requests for the onboarding checklist saw intermittent 429s for a subset of requests; most users retried and succeeded.
- We did not change our client behavior; no sudden burst from our side on request volume (checked).

Attached: short extract of our client logs and the failing request IDs we captured.

Appreciate a quick fix; this blocks a scheduled customer demo at 10:30.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Alex Stone <alex.stone@orchidanalytics.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 10:05:47 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected 429s from Orchid — initial notice

Hi all — quick technical summary and immediate mitigations.

Root cause (short): a config drift during a recent rollout caused a newer rate-limiter policy to be applied to Orchid’s tenant identifier. The policy had a lower per-minute allowance for burst tokens than the prior policy. The drift is in a merged policy bundle where a fallback key was accidentally re-mapped. We’ve reproduced the behavior in staging by applying the bundle and running a synthetic sync.

What we did (immediate):
- Rolled back the policy bundle affecting Orchid at 09:18 PDT which restored the previous rate window and removed the unexpected 429s.
- Re-routed traffic to a conservative fallback policy for any residual anomalous keys while we validate the bundle.
- Collected traces for the 08:40–09:20 window and attached the request traces and diff (rate-limiter-config.diff.txt).

Customer-facing mitigations you can apply (Alex):
- If you see persistent client retries causing duplicate work, add idempotency keys to the sync job payloads for the short term.
- If you must, reduce client retry aggression (exponential backoff with jitter) while we validate.

Next steps (follow-up plan):
1) Full postmortem + timeline (w/ root cause and corrective actions) by Tue 2027-05-25 EOD.
2) Policy rollout hardening: add an automated policy-compatibility checker and pre-flight that tests tenant-mapped allowances.
3) Add an alert for policy-drift anomalies that triggers an on-call page and a tenant-impact dashboard.

We’ll run the compatibility checker against the current bundles and share results by Monday.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this interrupted your demo. We’ll offer a goodwill credit for downtime and will follow up via CS with details.

-Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: rate-limiter-config.diff.txt; repro-run-logs.tar.gz
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Stone <alex.stone@orchidanalytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: 429 incident, postmortem and customer remediation plan

Alex — following our earlier notes and Karthik’s technical summary, here are the customer-facing artifacts and next steps we promised.

What happened (brief): a policy bundle rollout introduced an unintended mapping for Orchid’s tenant key. The mis-mapped policy reduced burst allowances and caused elevated 429s from ~08:52–09:18 PDT on 2027-05-22. We rolled that bundle back and applied a temporary routing to the conservative fallback while verifying.

Customer remediation provided:
- Immediate rollback and routing change (completed 09:18 PDT 2027-05-22).
- Config diff showing the exact change (attachment: rate-limiter-config.diff.txt).
- Trace logs from our side capturing failed and successful request IDs (attachment: request-trace-20270522-0900.jsonl).
- Recommended client mitigations (idempotency keys, reduced retry aggressiveness).

Operational corrective actions we will take:
- Automated compatibility pre-flight for policy bundles (target: deploy Q3 2027).
- Drift-detection alerting and a tenant-impact dashboard (target: deploy Q2 2027).
- Post-deployment 24-hour audit window for policy changes that affected >1% of tenants.

We’re also issuing a one-time service credit to Orchid for the incident; Neha from CS will follow up with the credit paperwork and any additional support for the replay of your demo.

If you need a technical call to walk through the traces and the config diff, Karthik and I are available Wed morning. Otherwise, we’ll mark this incident resolved and send the formal postmortem on Tue EOD as noted.

Thanks again for your patience — sorry for the impact.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
